To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the lateral spiriform (SpL) nucleus contains enkephalin immunoreactivity and that it projects to layers 8-13 of the tectal neuropil.

(1) there are enkephalineric fibers in all layers of the tectal neuropil, (2) the enkephalingeric fibers in layers 3‐5 may be intrinsic to the tectom, (3) the enkeplalineric fibers of layers 8‐13 are derived from the lateral spiriform nuclei, (4) the enkepbalingeric fibers of layers are derived from the enkepahalingeric cells

the avian lateral pretectal nucleus (SpL), the nucleus of origin of the tectofugal pathway, contains enkephalin, and that SpL projects to the tecta in a pattern that corresponds to the enkephalingeric fibers in the tecta.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the enkepahalin system in the avian basal ganglia.
the enkephalins in the avian tecta and with the possible influence of the basal ganglia over the tectum.
the role of the basal ganglia in the regulation of motor behavior and with the neural mechanisms by which the basal ganglia influence motor behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there exists an enkephalingeric projection to the tecto‐spino‐lencephalic system.
there are at least two distinct enkephalin patterns in the pigeon tecta, and that the pattern of fibers in layers 3–7 is independent of that in layers 8 –13.
the enkephalins are not the only transmitter substances in the avian tecta, but that they do have a role to play in tectal function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
enkephalin has a role in the basal ganglia control of the optic tectal system in birds.
the basal ganglia have an enkephalineric influence on the avian tecta.
the enkephalins in the tectal neurons are involved in motor functions of the tectal output, and the enkephals in the SpL neurons are involved in sensory functions of the tetal inputs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the enkephalins are involved in the modulation of tectal motor output.
we have identified an enkephalingeric projection to the optic tectal layers of origin of major tectal motor outputs.
we found that the enkephalins are involved in the control of the optic tectal layers.
